original_value: In this paper, an improved particle swarm optimization method (PSO) is proposed to optimally size and place a DG unit in an electrical power system so as to improve voltage profile and reduce active power losses in the system. An IEEE 34 distribution bus system is used as a case study for this research. A new equation of weight inertia is proposed so as to improve the performance of the PSO conventional algorithm. This development is done by controlling the inertia weight which affects the updating velocity of particles in the algorithm. Matlab codes are developed for the adapted electrical power system and the improved PSO algorithm. Results show that the proposed PSO algorithm successfully finds the optimal size and location of the desired DG unit with a capacity of 1.6722 MW at bus number 10. This makes the voltage magnitude of the selected bus equal to 1.0055 pu and improves the status of the electrical power system in general. The minimum value of fitness losses using the applied algorithm is found to be 0.0.0406 while the average elapsed time is 62.2325 s. In addition to that, the proposed PSO algorithm reduces the active power losses by 31.6%. This means that the average elapsed time is reduced by 21% by using the proposed PSO algorithm as compared to the conventional PSO algorithm that is based on the liner inertia weight equation.

result.paraphrase: The paper proposes an improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) approach for optimally sizing and locating a DG unit in an electrical power system to enhance voltage profile and cut active power losses. The study uses the IEEE 34 distribution bus system as a case study. To boost the performance of the standard PSO algorithm, a new inertia-weight equation is introduced by controlling the inertia weight that influences particle velocity updates. Matlab codes are developed for the modified power system model and the enhanced PSO method. The results indicate that the proposed PSO algorithm successfully identifies the optimal DG size and placement, with a capacity of 1.6722 MW at bus 10. This raises the voltage magnitude at the selected bus to 1.0055 pu and improves the overall condition of the electrical power system. The minimum fitness-loss value obtained with the applied algorithm is 0.0406, and the average elapsed time is 62.2325 s. In addition, the proposed PSO algorithm reduces active power losses by 31.6%. Compared with the conventional PSO algorithm based on the linear inertia-weight equation, the average elapsed time is reduced by 21%.
